news.title: UEFA to boycott World Cup if Infantino sell-off plan goes ahead
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. England, its fellow UEFA nations and CONCACAF have unanimously voted to boycott the upcoming men’s and women’s World Cups if Gianni Infantino goes ahead with plans to sell off shares in the tournament to private investors. UEFA’s 55 member nations held a virtual crisis meeting on Thursday to discuss Infantino’s recently announced plans to privatise and sell shares in the World Cup.

news.title: Fifa not ‘selling football’ as Uefa vows World Cup boycott over Infantino plan
news.lede: Uefa members voted unanimously on Thursday to boycott future World Cups if Fifa moves forward with plans to sell stakes in its competitions to private investors. Hours later, the Confederation of North, Central American and Caribbean Association Football (Concacaf) announced that its 41 members were also opposed to Fifa’s ⁠proposal. The decision by Uefa’s 55 member nations to “unequivocally reject” Fifa ⁠president Gianni Infantino’s recent plan was made during an emergency virtual meeting. On Friday, however, the world governing body issued a statement denying it was “selling football” and doubled down on it plans to launch a consultation process on the move.

news.title: 'Nobody is selling football!' - FIFA responds to controversy and offers explanation after Gianni Infantino's World Cup plan sparks outrage
news.lede: FIFA has issued a firm response to the mounting backlash surrounding its controversial World Cup spin-off proposal, insisting that "nobody is selling football." The governing body claims media reports mischaracterised the plans and reaffirmed its commitment to a democratic process. FIFA has officially responded to the fierce opposition surrounding its proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) project. The governing body released a public statement attempting to clear up what it described as "incorrect media reports" that disrupted the planned consultation process.

news.title: AFC 'stands in solidarity' with Uefa and Concacaf over Fifa World Cup plans
news.lede: The Asian Football Federation (AFC) has become the latest governing body to come out in opposition against Fifa's controversial private investment scheme. Fifa insist it will be pushing ahead with a consultation process about whether to sell off stakes in the World Cup and its other tournaments to private investors, despite widespread criticism of the proposal. The pushback since football's world governing body revealed its plan to sell a 20 per cent stake in a subsidiary company set up to run Fifa's competitions has been relentless. And now the AFC has joined the growing chorus of disapproval which had already reached fever pitch on Thursday when Uefa, European football's governing body, announced that they will boycott the World Cup – and all Fifa's competitions – if the plan of president Gianni Infantino was not scrapped.

news.title: FIFA insists 'nobody is selling football' after UEFA threatens to boycott tournaments if plans to sell off stake in World Cup go ahead
news.lede: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has described Gianni Infantino as "the wrong man" to lead FIFA, increasing the pressure on world football's president after a key advisor resigned over his controversial plans. Burnham denounced FIFA's proposal to sell stakes in its competitions - including the World Cup - to private investors when the news first emerged and on Friday said: "The idea that [the plan] could even be brought forward shows that, in my view, [he] is the wrong man to lead the organisation." Burnham's criticism came after the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) joined UEFA and CONCACAF in its opposition and called for "FIFA to undertake an urgent review of its governance". In a further damaging development, Carlos Cordeiro, a senior advisor to Infantino, resigned in protest at the privatisation plan, saying it was a "bad deal for football" and "for the long-term future of the game".

news.title: Bayern Munich’s goalscorer Aleksandar Pavlović wants to move on from World Cup debacle after dominant friendly win
news.lede: Aleksandar Pavlović is choosing to look forward rather than dwell on Germany’s disappointing World Cup campaign. Reflecting on the tournament, the Bayern Munich midfielder made it clear that he is using the experience as motivation rather than allowing it to define him. “You have to take positives from every setback. Now I’m just looking forward to the season so I can show what I can do and achieve success with the team,” Pavlović said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia).

news.title: Fifa is studying impact of expanding World Cup to 64 teams for 2030 edition, document says
news.lede: Governing body commissions study into potential 64-team World Cup expansion. Fifa is studying the impact ​of expanding the ‌World Cup from 48 to 64 teams ​for the ​2030 edition, according to ⁠a document seen ​by Reuters. "Fifa wishes ​to appoint an independent agency to determine whether ​and how expanding ​the FIFA World Cup ‌from 48 to 64 participating national teams, starting with the ​2030 edition, ​would ⁠impact on the tournament ​proposition," it said ​in ⁠a research brief.
